records.deidentified_narrative: when i arrived at v-1's home, she was walking slowly to the front gate and stated she had a bad hip and it was the same one that got bumped at the incident location by s1. v-1 stated she and w1 were walking out of the dollar tree and crossing through the private lot when s-1, who was driving listed vehicle, [roadway] l at a high rate of speed and bumped v-1. v-1 approached s-1 and informed her that she had hit her and didn't appear to attempt to avoid hitting her. v-1 asked s-1 for her insurance information, however, v-1 said s-1 refused to give her the information and said she would talk to the police when then got there. v-1 stated she began feeling pain and wanted to go home, thus leaving the incident location. v-1 advised me that there was a witness and was able to provide me with the information for w2. i called w2 who stated she was sitting in her car a few parking stalls away and saw v-1 and w-1 walking and when she looked up, she noticed the vehicle occupy a stall at the same time observing v-1 stumble. w2 addressed v1 to see if she was ok and and v-1 to her that the van had hit her. w2 stated it seemed that s1 did not have any regard for pedestrians and was turning into the spot carelessly. both w2 and v1 described s1 as a female in her mid 60's to mid 70's, short, wavy (pixie cut), salt and pepper hair, about 5'5"", with a thin build. v1 was asked if she would like to be checked out by ems and she accepted. engine 13 made location and cleared v1. i did not observe any fresh bruising or abrasions at the reported point of impact at this time. i contacted tid rendon #2417 who advised me to document as failure to render aid-moving and to document as a hit and run and the crash report. v1 was provided [case id] and follow up unit information. coban/bwc avail

records.public_safe_text: i arrived to the dispatched location responding to a call for an accident major involving a pedestrian. i observed unit 2 (pedestrian) laying on the sidewalk and no signs of unit 1. unit 2 did not have any visible injuries and no signs of major trauma. i asked unit 2 to tell me what happened and he said he had been hit. apart from saying he had been hit, unit 2 was not providing any other information when asked what direction he was coming from or what direction he was going in when he got hit. unit 2 could not provide any description whatsoever for unit 1. unit 2 could not tell me what color the traffic signal light was when he was hit and could not tell me what part of the roadway he was in when he was hit. i asked unit 2 what he was doing in the roadway at this time during dark hours and unit 2 said he is homeless. i did not observe any vehicle debris in the roadway and did not see any skid marks. i did not detect any odor of intoxicants coming from unit 2. as i looked at where unit 2 was on the sidewalk i observed a sweater in the roadway and a bottle of cologne and a lighter and other clothing items several feet away from unit 2. i spoke with others at an open laundry mat near the intersection and was told by a 911 caller that he heard a sound like a dog being hit and then looked toward the intersection and observed a truck which is believed to have been unit 1 drive away from the [roadway] and then he saw unit 2 laying on the ground and heard him moaning. the 911 caller could not provided any other description for unit 1. ems checked unit 2 at the scene and found unit 2 had minor injuries. unit 2 was complaining of pain to his [medical facility] as a precautionary measure. i spoke with det. groce# 2530 regarding the call. the scene and unit 2 were processed [medical facility]. bwc/coban ava.
